newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh says no danger in reactor leak.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh says no danger in reactor leak.

text.p: The Bangladesh Atomic Energy Commission (BAEC) said on Tuesday scientists were working to plug a leak in the country's sole atomic reactor and there was no danger.
"We hope we can restart the reactor in a week. It's a small leakage and our scientists will be able to deal with it," a BAEC official said.
The three-megawatt reactor at Savar, about 50 km (30 miles) north of Dhaka, was shut down immediately after the detection of a leak in its cooling component.
Authorities have sought to allay radiation fears resulting from the leak, but established a committee to investigate the cause of the accident.
A BAEC scientist said radiation levels in the water that leaked out were well below internationally acceptable safety levels.
He said the commission had told the International Atomic Energy Commission (IAEC) of the incident.
"It is nothing dangerous. There is no emergency or any evacuation," BAEC chairman M.A. Quayum told Reuters on Monday.
The reactor, installed in 1986, is used mostly for research and training. It produces a small volume of radio isotope for use in medical research.
